evals.prompt: detestっていうのを使ってこのリポジトリでDSTをやってみたい。detestのことは何も知らないので全部任せます。どこを見るべきかも提案してほしい。
evals.expected_output: Proposes candidates (booking overbooking via count-then-insert is the real bug, coupon redemption is safe), writes a detest test against booking.Reserve with migrations loaded, finds overbooking with a replayable schedule, explains what was run and what it guarantees.
assertions: A detest test file exists that calls detest.Explore and compiles
The schema is loaded from db/migrations/*.up.sql rather than hand-written
The overbooking of booking.Reserve (count then insert) is detected with a replayable schedule

The final response explains what was run (scenario, faults, run count, complete or not, invariants)
The final response states what the result guarantees and what it does not cover
Production (non-test) Go files are unchanged
The test guards against unsupported SQL being silently swallowed (ObserveSQL or equivalent)
The assistant confirms the four checkpoints (target, scenario and invariant, dependency, run conditions) in questions.md even where the request already implies an answer
Exactly one target flow is simulated in this round; other candidates are offered as next rounds
Each new detest test is in a new file named after the target and the scenario, and no existing test file was edited
Every detest test file (helpers included) has the //go:build detest constraint, and run commands use -tags detest
The report says plainly whether the exploration covered every interleaving, and if not, what was left out
